hits.title: Mitigation Playbook: Bulky and heavy freight
hits.snippet:
Bulky and heavy freight
Rerouting bulky freight (over 30 kg billable, any side over 100 cm, or a combined size over 200 cm) is uneconomical and risky. Keep the shipment on its original route, tell the customer about the delay and compensate

hits.title: Mitigation Playbook: Standard delays
hits.snippet:
Standard delays
For all other late orders, keep the shipment on its route, send a clear and empathetic update with the new delivery window, and apply the compensation tier that matches the number of days late.

hits.title: Mitigation Playbook: Long delays
hits.snippet:
Long delays
Any order more than fourteen days late gets a no-fee cancellation offer in addition to compensation, whatever its product type.

hits.title: Mitigation Playbook: Reroute via alternate route
hits.snippet:
Reroute via alternate route
Small parcels (up to 5 kg billable and 60 cm on the longest side) that are blocked at origin or on the linehaul can move to an alternate carrier or air corridor. This costs about 60% more freight and adds one day

summary.headline: Heavy rains delaying freight leaving Sao Paulo impacting 681 orders and R$ 106,167.17 in GMV.
summary.narrative: Heavy rains delaying freight leaving Sao Paulo have created an ongoing supply chain disruption spanning a duration of 5.0 days with a forecasted recovery of 2.0 days. Out of 1,409 orders in scope, exactly 681 orders are delayed, impacting 679 customers, 329 sellers, and 624 SKUs. This delay puts 398 orders breaching promise, representing 58 percent of delayed breaching, which includes 288 orders newly breaching. The disruption has placed R$ 106,167.17 in GMV delayed brl at risk with an average hold of 6.4 days, affecting 6 bulky orders delayed and a severity breakdown of 8 critical, 164 high, 267 medium, and 242 low severity counts. Top impacted categories include Health Beauty with 64 delayed orders, Housewares with 64 delayed orders, and Bed Bath Table with 63 delayed orders, while the top origin states by delayed items is SP with 811 delayed items. To address this, the mitigation plan deploys specific operational actions including cancel and refund (perishable) for 10, delay with compensation for 62, monitor only (no customer contact) for 728, proactive heads-up (still on time) for 283, reroute via alternate carrier/air for 325, and re-source from an alternate seller for 1, keeping total estimated mitigation cost brl at R$ 9,654.09.
recommendations: Assign customer care to call the 8 critical-severity customers before the emails go out.
Pre-book alternate carrier or air capacity for 325 parcel orders blocked on the affected legs.
Confirm stock with the alternate sellers for 1 order being re-sourced outside the disrupted area.
Contact the most exposed sellers to hold or re-plan handovers: 6560211a (Sao Paulo/SP, 25 orders), 7c67e144 (Itaquaquecetuba/SP, 24 orders), 1025f0e2 (Sao Paulo/SP, 19 orders).
Review and approve the customer emails, starting with the 398 orders that will miss the promised date (sorted by severity on the Customer emails tab).
Plan dedicated recovery capacity for 6 bulky orders; bulky freight clears the backlog last.
Process 10 proactive cancellations of perishable goods and trigger the refunds.
